metadata.title: Design a global Feature Flag platform
metadata.description: Resolve the decisions that materially change evaluation latency, consistency, failure behavior, privacy, and multi-region operations.

questions.prompt: What should the data plane optimize for when the control plane or network is unavailable?

options.label: Availability first with bounded staleness
options.description: Continue evaluating from the last verified snapshot and expose its age.

options.label: Consistency first
options.description: Reject evaluation when fresh configuration cannot be confirmed.

options.label: Per-flag failure policy
options.description: Let each flag choose stale, default-off, or error behavior.

questions.recommendationRationale: Feature evaluation commonly sits on critical request paths, so a verified stale snapshot is safer than turning a control-plane incident into a global application outage.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if a regulated workload requires proof of immediate revocation for specific flags.

questions.prompt: Where should production flag evaluation run?

options.label: In-process SDK
options.description: Applications evaluate locally from signed, versioned configuration snapshots.

options.label: Sidecar or node-local daemon
options.description: A local service centralizes evaluation and snapshot distribution per host or cluster.

options.label: Remote evaluation API
options.description: Applications call a regional service for each evaluation.

questions.recommendationRationale: Local evaluation removes a network hop from hot paths and preserves availability during regional control-plane failures.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if supported runtimes cannot safely implement identical rule semantics.

questions.prompt: What propagation guarantee should operators receive after publishing a flag change?

options.label: Bounded eventual consistency
options.description: Publish a target propagation SLO and show per-region convergence status.

options.label: Globally ordered activation
options.description: Do not acknowledge publication until all required regions can observe one committed version.

options.label: Tiered consistency
options.description: Use bounded eventual consistency normally and stronger coordination for emergency flags.

questions.recommendationRationale: Most flags benefit from fast regional propagation, while kill switches justify a narrower, stronger operational path.

defer.validationTrigger: Measure real propagation tails across three regions and validate emergency-change requirements with incident responders.

questions.prompt: How much user or tenant data may enter the evaluation engine?

options.label: Typed context evaluated locally
options.description: SDKs evaluate approved attributes in process and do not send raw context to the platform.

options.label: Pseudonymous identifiers only
options.description: Allow stable hashed IDs for percentage rollout and cohort membership.

options.label: Centralized context service
options.description: Upload targeting attributes to support server-side evaluation and analysis.

questions.recommendationRationale: Keeping evaluation context inside the application minimizes privacy exposure and removes a global user-profile dependency.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit only when a required targeting use case cannot be expressed with locally available approved attributes.

questions.prompt: How should configuration reach globally distributed SDKs?

options.label: Regional streams with polling fallback
options.description: Regional relays push version notifications; SDKs fetch snapshots and poll when streams fail.

options.label: CDN snapshot polling
options.description: SDKs periodically fetch immutable snapshots from a global CDN.

options.label: Direct global streaming
options.description: Every SDK maintains a stream to the central control plane.

questions.recommendationRationale: Regional fan-out gives fast propagation without making persistent global connectivity the only recovery path.

defer.validationTrigger: Load-test connection fan-out and propagation SLO before committing to regional streaming infrastructure.

questions.prompt: What must an SDK verify before activating a new configuration snapshot?

options.label: Control-plane signature
options.description: Verify provenance and reject forged or corrupted snapshots.

options.label: Monotonic version
options.description: Reject accidental rollback unless explicitly authorized.

options.label: Schema and semantic validation
options.description: Reject malformed rules, missing defaults, and incompatible evaluator versions.

options.label: Transport checksum only
options.description: Rely on TLS and content checksums without a signed artifact.

questions.recommendationRationale: A bad global snapshot can affect every request path, so activation must be atomic and independently verifiable.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit only if a constrained runtime cannot support signature verification within startup and update budgets.

questions.prompt: How should flag writes work across regions?

options.label: Single writer with regional failover
options.description: Route writes to one home region and promote a standby through a controlled failover.

options.label: Multi-region consensus
options.description: Accept writes in several regions through one globally ordered log.

options.label: Project ownership by region
options.description: Assign each project a write region while replicating reads globally.

questions.recommendationRationale: Configuration writes are low volume; a single ordered authority simplifies auditability, versioning, and conflict handling without affecting local evaluation.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if control-plane write availability cannot meet the agreed operator SLO during a regional outage.

questions.prompt: Which safeguards should be mandatory for high-impact flag changes?

options.label: Progressive rollout stages
options.description: Increase exposure through explicit, observable stages.

options.label: Metric-triggered rollback
options.description: Revert when linked guardrail metrics breach thresholds.

options.label: Second-person approval
options.description: Require review for production or emergency-class changes.

options.label: Change windows
options.description: Restrict high-impact changes to staffed operating windows.

questions.recommendationRationale: A global control surface needs both blast-radius reduction and a fast automated escape path; approval protects against operator error.

defer.validationTrigger: Enable automatic rollback after each service defines reliable, low-noise guardrail metrics.

questions.prompt: How should rule semantics evolve across many SDK languages?

options.label: Versioned rule IR with conformance suite
options.description: Publish a language-neutral evaluator contract and certify SDKs against shared vectors.

options.label: Server-compiled lookup tables
options.description: Compile rules centrally into simpler runtime-specific artifacts.

options.label: Independent SDK implementations
options.description: Document behavior and let each language evolve separately.

questions.recommendationRationale: Local evaluation is only trustworthy when identical context produces identical results across supported runtimes.

defer.validationTrigger: Validate the IR against the first three SDK languages and measure evaluator complexity before freezing version 1.

questions.prompt: What evaluation telemetry should the platform collect by default?

options.label: Sampled aggregate counters
options.description: Report flag/version/result counts without raw targeting context.

options.label: Per-evaluation events
options.description: Emit detailed decision events for debugging and experimentation.

options.label: Operational health only
options.description: Collect snapshot age, errors, and SDK health but no evaluation results.

questions.recommendationRationale: Aggregates support rollout health and adoption analysis while limiting cost, cardinality, and privacy exposure.

defer.validationTrigger: Approve aggregate dimensions through privacy review and load-test telemetry volume at projected peak evaluations.

questions.prompt: How strongly should the platform enforce flag cleanup?

options.label: Owner and expiry required
options.description: Every temporary flag has an owner, expiry, reminders, and escalation.

options.label: Advisory lifecycle metadata
options.description: Recommend ownership and expiry without blocking creation.

options.label: External governance
options.description: Leave cleanup policy to service teams and inventory tooling.

questions.recommendationRationale: Stale flags compound evaluator complexity and operational ambiguity; lifecycle metadata is cheapest to capture at creation.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit enforcement only if onboarding data shows it blocks legitimate long-lived operational flags.

questions.prompt: What recovery path should exist for a bad global configuration or control-plane loss?

options.label: Immutable version history
options.description: Retain every published snapshot and its audit record.

options.label: Explicit signed rollback
options.description: Authorize SDKs to activate a prior version through a new monotonic command.

options.label: Offline emergency bundle
options.description: Distribute a separately controlled minimal kill-switch artifact.

options.label: Application defaults only
options.description: Rely on compiled defaults when no valid platform snapshot is usable.

questions.recommendationRationale: Recovery needs an auditable rollback that does not weaken monotonic version checks, plus application-owned defaults for total platform loss.

defer.validationTrigger: Run a game day that rolls back a globally published bad rule while the primary control region is unavailable.

questions.prompt: Should experimentation analytics be part of the initial platform boundary?

options.label: Separate experimentation integration
options.description: Expose stable assignments and events to a dedicated analytics system.

options.label: Built-in experimentation
options.description: Own assignment, exposure logging, metric computation, and statistical analysis.

options.label: No experimentation contract
options.description: Limit the platform to operational feature delivery.

questions.recommendationRationale: Flag delivery and statistical analysis have different data, privacy, and correctness concerns; a stable integration avoids coupling their release paths.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit after an experimentation owner defines exposure and assignment contracts.
